name: Heinrich Himmler
role: Reichsführer-SS, chief of the German police and a principal architect of the Holocaust (1900-1945)
summary: Himmler was an ideologue of racial nationalism who led the SS, the police and the concentration camp system and organised the extermination of the Jews. He held that blood and race decide worth, that Germans owe decency only to their own blood, that eastern peoples should be dispossessed, enslaved or removed and the East colonised, and that homosexuality and Christianity had to be fought. He demanded unconditional obedience to Hitler and described the SS as a racial and ideological elite order.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He created the SD to watch those with a 'bad conscience toward the Führer', as the pamphlet says, and built the Gestapo apparatus; the target was political enemies, not terrorism as such.

strong-leader.rationale: His 1936 pamphlet presents Hitler as sent by fate and demands unconditional obedience to the Führer and proper superiors.

empower-police-military.rationale: He built the SS, Gestapo and unified police under his command and expanded the Waffen-SS from three regiments to over 38 divisions.

rehabilitation.rationale: On homosexuals he said imprisonment does not change them and ordered them shot in camps; the camps he built used force and executions for obedience.

traditional-family.rationale: The pamphlet makes the SS marriage law, clan and the 'sacred duty' of the mother central, but he also backed Lebensborn for unmarried mothers and wanted to replace the Christian concept of marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He called homosexuality a threat to the nation's survival (Bad Tölz, 1937) and said anyone who thinks of homosexual love is an enemy, per a 1928 note quoted by the sourcebook.

abortion-legal.rationale: He founded the Reich Central Office for Combating Homosexuality and Abortion in 1936 and urged high birth rates for the 'right' stock.

more-religion-public.rationale: He wanted Christianity overcome and Germanic ceremonies in public and SS life, while saying the SS believes in God; this points both ways.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The pamphlet praises ancestors, runes, ancient law, the plough and graves and urges veneration of ancestors.

gradual-change.rationale: He wanted the SS to overcome Christianity within a half-century and to colonise the East 'without any question of old traditions but with revolutionary impetus'.

nation-first.rationale: At Posen he said concern is only for 'our people and our blood' and 'we can be indifferent to everything else'.

one-party-rule.rationale: He tied the SS to the NSDAP and built its police arm as the 'executioner's sword' guarding the Nazi state against rival movements; he describes parliamentary parties' rule as a stage toward Bolshevism.

democracy-best.rationale: His pamphlet describes the rule of democratic-bourgeois parties and then moderate socialists as stages of a Jewish-Freemason path to Bolshevism, and he built the police state that ended Weimar democracy.

natural-rulers.rationale: At Posen he said the SS-farmer elite would give Europe its 'leading class', and the pamphlet praises a 'ruling class' of the best blood.

political-violence-never.rationale: At Posen he said the SS did not hesitate to shoot comrades on 30 June 1934 and would do it again, and he organised mass killing.

war-builds-character.rationale: At Posen he wanted every SS division to spend a winter in the East every second or third year so the SS 'never grow soft'.

separate-church-state.rationale: The pamphlet draws a 'sharp and distinct line' between church activity and political world-view soldiery, but his anti-church campaign aimed to subordinate the churches, not neutral separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred: he called Christianity a plague and wanted Germanic values as the base of law; his pamphlet treats the Bible as Jewish history.

military-superiority.rationale: He expanded the Waffen-SS and told his commanders Germany needed 20-30 intact SS divisions at armistice talks.

ethnic-nation.rationale: At Posen he said the SS man must be loyal and comradely only to 'members of our own blood' and sought to push the Germanic border 5,000 km east.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He saw history as a struggle between humans and sub-humans led by Jews, not between classes.

self-interest-moral.rationale: At Posen he told the SS not to enrich themselves with a Mark or a watch, and set duty to the people above personal gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The pamphlet puts the 'minuteness of the individual's own mortal self' below clan and folk, and at Posen he said 'our duty is our people and our blood'.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The pamphlet praises ancient Germanic law that protected trees and animals as 'created by God' and having a soul.

limit-population.rationale: He wanted copious breeding of the 'racial super-stratum' and said the German child's victory must follow the victory of arms.

restore-past-order.rationale: Longerich reports he wanted to restore a 'Germanic way of living', but he also pressed new SS institutions and conquest.

harm-principle.rationale: He rejected homosexuals' view that sex is private, saying all sexual matters concern 'the life and death of the nation'.

conscription.rationale: At Posen he said the SS would 'legally draft youth of all ages' after the war, and in 1944 he helped raise the Volkssturm drafting males 16-60.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He wrote that Germanic blood is 'the best blood', that enemies had 'inferior blood', and he rejected Slavs as racially inferior.

national-rebirth.rationale: The pamphlet casts Hitler as ending a 2,000-year path of defeat and moving the folk to 'the beginning of its mission'.

territorial-expansion.rationale: At Posen he spoke of pushing the national boundary 5,000 km east to the Urals and imposing German laws on the East.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The pamphlet makes loyalty to the Führer the SS's ground ('All honour comes from loyalty') and asserts a personal oath unto death.

universal-morality.rationale: He said the SS owe decency only to their own blood and that nothing else concerns them.

national-self-determination.rationale: At Posen he said giving Czechs and Slovenes national consciousness was a mistake, and his 1940 memo aimed to dissolve eastern peoples' national concepts.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He says loyalty is 'a matter of the heart, never of the mind' and that the SS can only be understood with 'blood and heart'.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He drove the ban on sex between Germans and foreign workers as 'race defilement', ran ghettos and camps, and enforced racial classification; I did not find him drafting a residence and schooling segregation law.

national-mission.rationale: In 1942 he said it was the mission of 'this blond race' to rule the earth and create a Germanic Reich 'blessing for the earth'; he did not address spreading a form of government.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: he spoke of selection and racial hygiene and of breeding the SS like a breeder purifying a strain, but I opened no statement of his on defective births.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The pamphlet says peoples die from 'endless race-mixing', and his SS marriage order required proof of Aryan descent to 1800.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: At Posen he said honesty and decency are owed only to members of one's own blood, and he called Slavs 'human animals'.

population-transfer.rationale: His 1940 memo wanted all Jews removed to Africa, other eastern peoples 'dissolved', and he led deportations and Germanisation of Polish lands.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He launched and directed mass killing, wars of conquest and a campaign of deportation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The pamphlet calls the struggle between 'humans and sub-humans' a law of nature and says the law of the world counts 'who triumphs'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: he held that race-mixing degrades peoples and wanted an ethnically pure nation, but no statement about diversity and cohesion was found.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: As chief of police he ran protective custody and camp detention outside ordinary legal protection against 'enemies of the state', and in the pamphlet promised the SS would crush any attempted uprising.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: At Posen he called Slavs 'human animals' to be used as slaves for German culture, and in the pamphlet ranked Germanic culture above others.

death-penalty.rationale: He ordered homosexuals shot after sentences in camps, threatened SS thieves with death 'without mercy', and led an apparatus of executions; most were extrajudicial.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: His Volksliste classified people of 'German blood' and he insisted on blood descent as the base of the national community.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He told SS leaders in 1942 that Christianity must be dealt with 'in a tougher way' and called it the greatest of plagues, but I found no stated policy on church property or clergy law.

character-from-environment.rationale: The pamphlet makes blood and selection the basis of character and tests; he said unfit sons would be removed for lack of 'blood'.

leader-cult.rationale: He closed the Posen speech with a paean to the Führer and the pamphlet says fate sent Hitler; he did not himself discuss portraits or statues.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: At Posen he spoke of a Germanic Reich under which the 'Germanic people', with 250-300 million, would lead Europe.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He called it 'a crime against our own blood' to give subject peoples 'ideals' and valued them only as slaves and labour.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The pamphlet praises Germanic law for giving animals rights and at Posen he claimed Germans are the only people with a decent attitude to animals.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He founded Lebensborn welfare for mothers of 'racially valuable' children and pressed for large families; financial state incentives specifically are not documented in sources opened.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The pamphlet demands 'unconditional obedience' to Hitler or any proper superior, 'obedience unto death'.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The pamphlet says Jews organise Bolshevism, freemasonry and revolutions with a 'wish for world domination' and 'will to extermination'.

defeat-communism.rationale: The pamphlet states the SS would be a 'pitiless executioner's sword' against Jewish-Bolshevik revolution, and he called the war in the East a crusade against 'Godless Bolshevik hordes'.

religion-illusion.rationale: He held a theistic faith in God and fate (Wralda) and said non-believers are arrogant and dumb, so he did not treat religion as an illusion.

majority-settlement.rationale: As Reich Commissioner for the Consolidation of German Nationhood he resettled ethnic Germans in Polish land, and at Posen he promised SS-farmer colonisation pushing the frontier east.

holocaust-denial.rationale: At Posen he stated openly that the extermination of the Jewish people was under way and justified it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In his 1937 Bad Tölz speech he ordered homosexual SS men expelled, jailed and shot in camps, and in 1936 created the Reich Central Office to combat homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He set up Dachau in March 1933 for political opponents and took over the Gestapo and all police, using camps and terror against opposition.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: At Posen he valued eastern nations only 'insofar as we need them as slaves for our culture'; these were land territories, not overseas ones.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The pamphlet says God 'has sent us our Führer' and demands oaths with 'So help us God', though he does not state the principle in general terms.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: For the SS and police he decreed public degradation, expulsion and a camp death sentence for homosexuals; this concerns his own forces, not other armies.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: His pamphlet quotes the SS catechism calling a person who does not believe in God 'arrogant, megalomaniac and dumb' and rejects being called atheist.

uniformed-youth.rationale: At Posen he planned to legally draft youth of all ages and to train them in arms and SS principles.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He praised the SS's readiness to kill and said at Posen that the SS had the 'moral right' to kill the Jews.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The pamphlet traces the folk from ancient Germanic ancestors with continuous 'eternal origins'.

person-over-state.rationale: At Posen he valued Russians as 'raw material' and labour and said their deaths mattered only for the anti-tank ditch.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The pamphlet frames history as a racial struggle and asks the SS to serve Germanic blood alone.

racial-pride.rationale: He called German blood the 'best blood' and wanted the SS to take pride in the 'value of our race and blood'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He planned Lebensraum conquest and helped stage the Operation Himmler pretext for invading Poland.

sacred-nation.rationale: He says the folk has eternal life through blood and clan and a divine mission, outlasting each person.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He denied equal humanity to Slavs and Jews, calling Slavs 'human animals' and Jews a 'bacillus'.

premarital-sex.rationale: Lebensborn took unmarried mothers (about 60 percent) if mother and father were 'racially valuable'; he did not otherwise endorse premarital sex.

race-social-construct.rationale: His SS selection rested on Nordic physical type and blood value, which he treated as real and graded.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He rejected Christianity as a plague and wanted a Germanic faith; he does not read scripture as inerrant.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The pamphlet says the SS blood concept is tied to 'the value and the holiness of the soil'.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: He led resettlement of ethnic Germans (the VoMi) and wanted 'German blood' abroad brought home or protected.

notes: Answers rely mainly on the 1936/37 SS pamphlet, the Posen speech of 4 October 1943, the Bad Tölz speech of 1937, the 1942 speech on Christianity and the 1940 memorandum. The Posen speech of 6 October 1943, the full 1940 memo, the diaries and Longerich's biography were not read directly. His 1940 memo called physical destruction of a people 'un-Germanic' but later policy included the Holocaust. The Posen full 115-page text, the 1935 Lebensborn order and the SS marriage order text were not opened; those points rest on Wikipedia.
